text: Nikhil, a retired teacher, had an urgent problem. His grandchildren were coming for dinner in one hour, and his good blue shirt was still in the washing machine. He grabbed his phone and typed fast, in lowercase: "how much time is left on the washng machine". The assistant checked and said the wash had twenty minutes to go. Nikhil asked it to track the cycle and tell him the moment it ended. A little later the phone chimed, and the assistant said the wash was done. Nikhil moved the shirt to the dryer and asked for a quick fifteen minute setting. The assistant started the dryer. When the doorbell rang, the shirt was warm and dry, and Nikhil was ready.

Sanne owned a small gift shop near the station, and tourists paid with coins and notes from many countries. One afternoon a man held up a vase that cost seventy euros and asked what that was in dollars. Sanne said to her phone, "What is seventy euros in US dollars right now?" The assistant looked up the exchange rate and said it was about seventy-six dollars. Sanne told the man, and he paid with a smile. Later, tired of the constant checking, she asked the assistant to alert her if the euro and dollar rate moved by more than two percent in a day. The assistant said it had set the alert. Sanne dropped a coin into the jar by the till and went back to work.

Most people use music to fill a room, to keep them company while they work, or to help them relax. What they change most is the volume, the song and the playlist. Volume works a little like a car brake: a small push slows things down, and a big push stops everything. So people say "turn it down", "a bit quieter, please" or "pause". To change the song they say "skip this one", "next song" or "play something else". For a playlist they might say "play my morning list" or "shuffle it". If you wish to hear one artist, say "play" and then the name. Even a silly old song is easy to find: just say the words you remember.

An air purifier is a small machine that pulls in the air of a room, cleans it, and sends it back out. People use it when the air smells bad or feels heavy, for example after cooking soup or frying fish, or when someone is sick or has allergies. Most people change only a few things: on or off, the fan speed, and a timer. They say "turn on the purifier", "make the air fresher", "set the fan to low at night" or "run it for two hours". A humidifier is a different machine. It adds a little water to dry air, so people say "make the room less dry". If a cycle ends too soon, they can say "repeat that" and the machine starts again.

A day at the beach needs a little planning. Sun cream protects your skin, and it wears off, so people ask for a reminder to put more on every two hours. The tide is the sea moving in and out twice a day. Swimming can be difficult when the tide is high or the waves are strong, so people ask "when is low tide?" or "is it safe to swim now?" Water temperature tells you how warm the sea is. Some people like to swim in warm water, and others only like to paddle. Many bring a flask of tea for afterwards. A good question to ask is "how warm is the sea today?"

name: line_check
does: Tells you whether a post office, bank or pickup counter is open and how long the line is, so you can stay home on an icy day, and it can send a signal when the line is short.
inputs: the place you want to visit and the time you plan to go; a welcome note with the closing time is shown at the end
people say:
- Is the post office still open?
- How long is the line at the bank right now?
- Can I collect my parcel today or is the counter shut?
- Tell me when the queue at the pickup point gets short.
- I don't want to wait outside in the cold, is it busy at the bank?

Television is for news, shows, films and sport. Most people change only a few things: the channel, the volume and sometimes the subtitles. Subtitles are the little words at the bottom of the screen. They help when the room is noisy, when a show is in another language, or when someone cannot hear well. People say "put the subtitles on", "I can't hear it, what does he mean?" or "turn the words off". To change the channel they say "go to channel five" or "put on the news". For streaming they say "play the next episode". After a camping trip, many families like to sit down and say "find a good film for tonight".

Ingrid was eight, and she wanted to cook pancakes for her mum's birthday. Her half finished puzzle of a lighthouse sat on the table, but the pancakes came first. The recipe was for four people, and Ingrid said to the kitchen speaker, "Make the recipe for two." The speaker gave her half of everything. Then Ingrid remembered. "Wait, no! Three people. Grandpa is coming too." The speaker changed its answer and said three quarters of the cups and spoons in the first list. It told her to use a small bowl and one egg plus a splash of milk. Ingrid measured everything, stirred, and carried the first warm pancake to her mum.

name: order_arrival_time
does: Tells you when your food order will arrive and where it lies on the way, and it says if a delay looks weird, longer than usual.
inputs: the restaurant name or the order number, and what you ordered, like a dozen dumplings
people say:
- Where is my food?
- How much longer until the pizza gets here?
- It's been an hour, has my order even left the restaurant?
- Is the driver close to my street?
- When will my dinner arrive?

A bank account is a safe place for your money, and the balance is how much is in it right now. Most people check their balance on a phone, and some move money between their own accounts, for example from a savings account to the one they spend from. They say "how much do I have?", "move fifty to savings" or "send twenty to my other account". If an account is almost empty, a small alert helps. If a card is lost, people say "freeze my card" so no one can use it. A sharp drop in the balance after a big bill is easy to see in the list of recent payments, and you can ask for that list too.

Fatima, a student, was packing for a weekend hike in the hills when her friends texted that they were leaving in ten minutes. It was urgent. She looked at her half empty bag and said to her phone, "What's the weather in the hills on Saturday, and what should I pack?" The assistant said it would be sunny by day but near freezing at night, with a light wind. It listed warm socks, a hat, a rain jacket and a second water bottle, and it took the cold night into account by adding a thin sleeping bag. Fatima took a deep breath, as if to breathe out the stress, and packed everything in five minutes.

Person: Good morning. I am moving to a smaller flat next month, and my back is not what it used to be, so I would be very grateful if you could help me find a moving company that carries boxes up the stairs.
Assistant: Of course. Which city are you moving in?
Person: Leeds. My flat is on the third floor and there is no lift.
Assistant: Thank you. What day would you like to move?
Person: The twelfth of next month. A low price would be nice, but kind helpers matter more.
Assistant: I can't book a company for you, but I can find movers in Leeds who work on the twelfth and show their prices and reviews. Shall I do that?
Person: Yes, please.

Person: Pool temperature.
Assistant: Which pool do you mean, the one at the front of the shop or the hot tub out the back?
Person: The front one. My aunt had it put in years ago.
Assistant: It is twenty-six degrees right now. Would you like me to change it?
Person: Drop it to twenty-four tonight.
Assistant: Done. I set the heater to twenty-four from this evening.
Person: Thanks.

Wendy, a cook, was writing the menu for her little restaurant. She had typed a line about grilled fish with garlic bulb butter, and she wanted every dish to sound delicious. She was not sure about one word and said to her laptop, "Spell vinaigrette." The assistant spelled it out letter by letter, and Wendy fixed her mistake. Then she said, "Word count." The assistant told her the menu had ninety-four words, which was too many for one small card. Wendy asked it to read the menu back, cut the longest dish name, and save the new version. The assistant did, and the card fit.

A phone is used for calls, messages, photos and maps, and it works only while the battery lasts. People change a few things often. Brightness is how bright the screen is. Outside in the sun the screen is hard to see, so people say "make the screen brighter", and at night they say "dim it". Battery saver makes the phone last longer, so they say "turn on battery saver". Do not disturb is like a small sign on your shirt collar that says you are busy: calls stay quiet until you say "turn off do not disturb". On a new phone you peel off the plastic film first. When storage is full, people say "delete my old photos".

name: wash_cycle_picker
does: Picks the right washing program for a bag of clothes and can choose a quiet cycle for the night.
inputs: what kind of clothes are in the bag, and whether the machine should be quiet; it should understand the care label words, like wool or delicate
people say:
- What setting do I use for wool?
- Wash my gym clothes, but keep it quiet, the baby is sleeping.
- Which cycle is best for towels?
- I have a bag of sheets that need washing tonight.
- How hot can I wash this shirt?

Person: How many days until my tomatoes are ready?
Assistant: When did you plant them?
Person: Seventeen days ago. My neighbour waved me over yesterday and said they often take about seventy days.
Assistant: Then they should be ready in about fifty-three days. Do you want a reminder?
Person: Yes, can you remind me in fifty days?
Assistant: Yes. Should I remind you in the morning?
Person: Morning is fine.

When you order something online, the shop packs it and gives you a tracking number. The tracking page shows where the parcel is and when it should arrive. People ask "where is my order?" or "when will it get here?" If the date changes, a good app will explain why, such as bad weather or a busy week. Sometimes people change the delivery day by saying "deliver it on Friday instead". If the parcel is wrong, they ask for a refund and say "I want my money back" or "send it back". On a phone, turn up the brightness to read the small code on the creamy white label inside the box.

Roya was a student planning a birthday party for her friend, and sixty people were coming. She stood in the hall with a pen and a very long list. First she said to her phone, "How do you spell congratulations?" so the banner would look right. The assistant spelled it out slowly, and she wrote it down. Next she asked it to make a playlist of happy songs for the party, and the assistant made one with forty songs. She also wanted a score sheet for the party game, but the weather news was bad and the party would be indoors. So she asked the assistant to remind her tomorrow to move the tables.

Person: Post my lunch photo.
Assistant: Which photo do you mean, and which account should I use?
Person: The one of the pan of roast potatoes. Delicious, right? Put it on my cooking page, not my work page.
Assistant: Got it. Do you want a caption?
Person: I don't want anything long. Just Sunday lunch.
Assistant: Posted to your cooking page with the caption Sunday lunch.

When you pay with a bank card, the money does not always leave your account at once. Sometimes the payment is only held for a day or two, and then it becomes final. This can confuse people, for example after buying theater tickets. If the bank takes the money twice, people often get angry and ask "why was I charged two times?" or "cancel the second payment". The transfer of money from one bank to another can drag on for a few days too. To check, people say "show my latest payments" or "is the money still pending?" A quick look at the list usually shows what is going on.

Hobbies and crafts give people something calm to do with their hands. An artist may paint, a knitter may make a scarf, and a child may build a model plane. Each hobby has small things people change: the colour, the size, the time it takes. A painter says "mix a darker green". A knitter says "I need a pair of needles in size five" or "how many rows are left?" A model builder asks "how long does the glue need to dry?" or "is it ready to paint?" Many people ask an assistant to set a timer, find a pattern, or order more paint, and they use plain words like "find me a simple pattern".

Ahmed was a grandfather who liked to read the news on his computer. One morning he sat down with his coffee, which was bitter, and a slice of toast. He opened a long article, but the screen was so dark that the words were hard to see. He said, "It's like reading in a cave in here." The assistant understood that he meant the screen was too dim. It turned up the brightness and asked, "Is that better?" Ahmed said it was better. Then he said the letters were still small, so the assistant made the text bigger. Ahmed smiled, ate his toast and read the whole article.

Food delivery lets you order a meal from a restaurant and have it brought to your door. You choose the dishes, give your address, and the app shows a time. People often add a special request, like no onions or extra sauce, and a tip for the driver. If the food is late, the app may warn you that the delay is longer than first said. A doctor on a night shift or a tired parent might say "order the same thing as last time" or "get dinner here in thirty minutes". To change an order, people say "make that two" or "add a tip of three dollars". It is easy when you use plain words.

They want to know how many days are left until a day on the calendar, such as a gold wedding anniversary, so no one has to cry about forgetting.
- days till christmas
- how many days are left untill my birthday
- How long until Friday?
- Count the days to our trip on June third.
- I can't read the calendar without my glasses, so how many days until the anniversary?
- Could you please tell me how many days remain before my sister's party?
- How far away is the end of the school year, in days?
- I would be grateful if you could work out how many days are left until the first of next month.

Valentina was a cook, and she looked after her grandmother on weekends. One evening, after she dropped a pot on the kitchen floor, she realised she was running late. She said to her smart speaker, "Remind my grandmother to take her pills at eight and call her at nine." The assistant said it would do both. It added that it would count the pills in the weekly list and tell her if one day was missing. Valentina had also looked at a medical alert bracelet, but it was expensive, so she asked the assistant to find cheaper ones. The assistant showed three, and Valentina saved the best one for later.

Bo was a gardener with a lemon tree and a very long list of friends. His neighbour had just given him a jar of lemon jam, so he wanted to add her to his phone. He said, "Add Maria Costa, phone 555 0142, and her birthday is the ninth of May." The assistant made the new contact. Then Bo frowned. "Sorry, her name is Marta, not Maria." The assistant fixed the name and kept the number and the birthday. Bo also asked it to remind him a week before the birthday so he could bring flowers and celebrate with her. The assistant set the reminder, and Bo went back to his lemon tree.

Callum woke up late and stared at the clock. He had a meeting across town in an hour. He rubbed his eyes and said to his phone, "How long does it take to drive to the office, and send the route to my car?" The assistant looked at the traffic website and said the drive would take thirty-five minutes, a little longer than usual because of road work. It sent the route to his car screen. Callum grabbed a piece of stale bread from the kitchen, put on his shoes and ran out the door. In the car, the route was already waiting for him, with the first turn shown on the screen.

Siti woke up at three in the morning to a quiet house. Her baby had been fussy with gas the night before, and she was not sure if the little one was still asleep. She whispered to her phone, "Start monitor." The assistant turned on the baby camera and showed a small, sleeping face. Siti sighed in relief. Then she asked, "Nap time?" The assistant told her the baby had last napped at noon and would probably want another nap at two. Siti asked it to skip the loud morning alarm and set a soft one instead. It was a simple fix, and she went back to bed.

They want help remembering a birthday and choosing a great gift for it.
- Gift ideas for my mum
- When is my gram's birthday, and what should I get her?
- I forgot last year, so remind me a week before Dad's birthday and suggest a present.
- What's a great present for a ten year old who likes drawing?
- Find me a card and remind me to post it
- Could you please remind me of my brother's birthday and suggest something under thirty dollars?
- Do I have any birthdays this month, and what could I give each person?
- I would love your help finding a gift for my teacher and a card to go with it.

Notes are a place to write down ideas before they fall out of your head. People use them for shopping lists, plans, a funny joke they want to remember, or a thought that came to them at night. Each note is an item in a list, and you can name it, change it or put it in a folder. Voice notes let you speak instead of type. People say "write this down", "make a note: call the dentist", "add milk to my shopping note" or "read me my last note". To find an old one they say "find the note about the garden". If a note is no longer needed, they say "delete that note".

Henry was a student, and he burned his finger on a hot pan while making dinner. It hurt, and he did not know what to do. He asked his phone, "What should I do for a small burn?" The assistant said to hold the finger under cool running water for ten minutes and not to use ice. Henry did that. The pain began to ease. Then he asked, "What is the price of burn cream at the shop?" The assistant found two kinds and said they cost a few dollars each. Henry put one on his personal shopping list and asked the assistant to remind him in ten days to check the burn again.

Kwame did not like phones much, and he talked to his assistant slowly. His daughter had ordered him a new skirt for his wife, and he was waiting for the delivery. He said, "Is there a parcel for me today, and what time does the post office shut?" The assistant checked and said the parcel was out for delivery and would come before six. The post office closed at five-thirty. It said that the maximum waiting time at the counter was usually ten minutes. Kwame thanked the assistant and sat on the porch to wait. When the van came, he smiled, signed his name, and carried the box inside.

Sunita had just moved to the city, and she wanted to send her mother some pictures of her new flat. She stood in the chilly bathroom and said to her phone, "Take a photo of the bathroom, and tomorrow morning remind me to take more." The assistant took a photo and set the reminder. Then Sunita said, "Create an album called New Home." The assistant made the album and put the photo in it. Later she asked it to share the album with her mother. The assistant sent the link, and a few minutes later her mother sent back a long row of happy faces.

Oscar woke up in the dark. The clock by his bed was off, and the whole flat was silent. He sat up and said, "It's pitch black in here and my phone is nearly dead." His phone assistant understood that he needed light and that the power might be out. It switched on the flashlight at a low level to save the weak battery, and it asked, "Do you want me to check if the power is out in your street?" Oscar said yes. The assistant said there was a power cut in the area and that the company expected to fix it by morning. Oscar thought about his diet food in the fridge and kept the door shut.

Person: whats the dose for ibuprofen
Assistant: I can help with that. Is it for an adult or a child?
Person: me, adult. my shoulder hurts from lifting boards all day at the shop
Assistant: Please check the box, because the right amount depends on the strength of your pills. I can't tell you a dose for your own body, but I can read the label if you tell me the strength.
Person: 200 mg
Assistant: The label for that kind says one or two pills with food, up to three times a day. If the pain sounds serious or stays thick and heavy for more than a few days, it is best to see a doctor. Do you want me to book an appointment?
Person: not now

Tesfaye was not good with technology, but his grandchildren had shown him how to talk to the kitchen speaker. One evening nineteen people were coming for his wife's party, and the cooking was behind. He said slowly, "Please order food for people. Something tasty." The speaker asked, "How many people, and what kind of food?" Tesfaye said, "Nineteen, and we like chicken." The speaker found a restaurant that could bring nineteen chicken meals in forty minutes. It told him the total and asked him to say yes. Tesfaye said yes. The speaker confirmed the order and the time, and Tesfaye went back to laying the table.

name: box_label_maker
does: Makes a label for each moving box with its room and contents, like a box of bulbs, and tells the movers where to put it.
inputs: what is inside the box and which room it goes to; you can also say if the stairs are icy so the movers know to take care
people say:
- Make a label for this box, it's all kitchen stuff.
- Where should the movers put the box of light bulbs?
- This one is for the bedroom, can you mark it fragile?
- Print stickers for my twelve boxes
- Which room does the box with my books go in?

Kenji had just moved to the city, and his first letter from the post office was a card saying a parcel was waiting. He picked up his phone and said, "I don't want to pay extra, and I don't want to wait in line. What is in the parcel?" The assistant said it was a black laptop battery that his brother had sent. Kenji frowned. He could not afford a long trip across town. The assistant found a pickup point two streets away that was free, and it said the parcel could be left at his door instead. Kenji chose the door and asked the assistant to tell him when it was delivered.

Bram, a teenager, was texting his friends when he remembered his hair. He said to his phone, "Book a haircut on Saturday morning and tell me when the barber opens." The assistant found a barber nearby that opened at nine and booked ten o'clock. Bram was saving money for a bike, so he asked the price, and the assistant said it was fifteen dollars for young people. Then he asked it to disconnect his phone from the loud speaker in the living room, because his dad was sleeping. The assistant did, and the house went quiet. Bram sent his friends a text saying he would be late to the park.

They want the lights turned down low, not switched off, for example when an excited girl wants to watch a film.
- Dim the lamp, but don't turn it off.
- Not so bright, please.
- Make the living room lights soft, I don't want total darkness.
- Can you lower the ceiling light to about twenty percent?
- Don't switch everything off, just leave the small light on.
- It's too bright to watch the film, could you turn it down a bit?
- I would like the lights low and warm, please, not white and sharp, because we are about to start.

They want to arrange a new delivery time for an order, maybe because fog or an average slow day made the first one late.
- Redeliver tomorrow
- Send it again on Friday.
- Can you change my delivery to the afternoon?
- I missed the courier, can they come back after five?
- Please arrange for the parcel to go to my neighbour's door.
- I won't be home on Monday, so could the driver come on Tuesday instead?
- I would be grateful if you could set up a different delivery day for my order, because I will be at work all week.

They want the heating to come on at a set time. The house should be warm and calm when the kids come in from their ball game, and the assistant can warn them if something fails.
- Turn the heating on at five.
- Start the radiators in two weeks when it gets colder.
- Have the house warm by six this evening.
- Can you heat the living room before we get home?
- Switch on the heating on the first of November, please.
- I would like the thermostat to go up to twenty-one degrees at half past four every weekday.
- Warm the house for the weekend, starting this Friday.

Stavros was a grandfather, and the summer was very hot. His grandchildren were coming to stay for the weekend, and the flat was stuffy. He said politely to the air conditioner, "Good morning. Could you please cool the bedroom to a lower level? My grandchildren are sleeping there this weekend, and they find it hard to rest when it is too warm." The assistant said it would set the room to twenty-two degrees and run the fan on low so it would not be loud. Stavros asked for it to be ready by six. It said yes. That evening there were many happy faces. He baked a cake while the room cooled.

Person: Plan my workout.
Assistant: Sure. How long do you have, and which part of your body do you want to work on?
Person: Twenty minutes. I just woke up and I'm still half asleep. I don't want anything hard.
Assistant: Understood. Do you want to do it at home or outside?
Person: At home. No weights, please. I'm feeling a bit sad today, so something easy.
Assistant: Here is a gentle plan: five minutes of stretching, ten minutes of slow squats and arm circles, then five minutes of walking in place. Should I count the sets for you?
Person: Yes, and ask me a question after each set to see how I feel.

Abdi was a gardener who got up early. He came into the kitchen with muddy boots, feeling sleepy, and said to the smart kitchen, "Make me a coffee." The coffee machine began to heat. Then he had another idea. "Wait, no, tea instead. Green tea." The assistant stopped the coffee machine and switched on the kettle. It said, "The kettle will be ready in two minutes." Abdi did a little dance on the doormat to get the mud off his boots, then sat down at the table. When the kettle clicked, the assistant told him the water was ready, and the tea was perfect.

Noah was a grandfather who loved riding the bus, and he wanted to visit his sister across town. He said to his phone, "When is the next bus thirteen?" The assistant said the next bus would arrive in twelve minutes. Noah asked it to forward the timetable to his sister, so she would know when he was coming. The assistant sent it. Then he said he rode the bus often, and he wanted a cheaper ticket. The assistant found a weekly pass that cost less than seven single tickets. Noah asked it to buy one, and he took a banana out of his bag for the ride.

They want a quick report of how many steps they have walked today, after a fresh morning walk, even if they have to shout it across the room.
- steps today
- How many steps have I done so far?
- What's my step count?
- Did I walk at least fifty minutes today?
- Tell me how far I walked this morning.
- Have I reached my goal of ten thousand steps?
- Could you please give me a summary of my walk, with distance and pace?
- I'd like to know how much I've moved today, if that's possible.

They want the car warmed up before they leave, because it is a pretty cold morning and the engine should sound smooth.
- warm up the car
- start my car in 5 minutes
- can u get the cra warm before I leave
- Heat up the car for ten minutes, please.
- Turn the engine on so it's warm when I come out.
- It's freezing, could you start the car and set the heater to high?
- I leave at eight, so please have the car warm by a minute before that.
- Would you mind starting my car in a few minutes so the windows clear?

Callum woke up with a sore knee, because he had been under the sink the night before. The tap was still dripping. He said to his phone, "Book a plumber for Tuesday." The assistant found a plumber and held the time. Then Callum remembered. "No wait, Wednesday. I'll be out on Tuesday." The assistant moved the booking to Wednesday morning. He also asked, "How much do I owe for a visit?" The assistant said the call out fee was sixty dollars. Callum asked it to remind him to leave the east door open on Wednesday so the plumber could get to the kitchen. The assistant set the reminder, and Callum went back to bed.
